Prevents falls. Protects technologists, nurses and patient escorts at the ultrasound exam table step from a minor or moderate injury.

Mounted on the wall at the exam table where staff see it before reaching the hazard.

Radiology managers, radiologic technologists, imaging center operations leads, hospital facilities and biomed.

Pinch Point At Chain Clasp. This CAUTION Cylinder Storage Chain sign from CGAP Safety reads: PINCH POINT / CYLINDER RESTRAINT CHAIN / KEEP FINGERS OUT OF CLASP. Written for chemical plants, specialty gas users, labs and process facilities.

Why this sign matters

Warns workers of a pinch point at cylinder storage chain so fingers and hands are kept clear of closing parts.

Where to post it

Mount on the wall bracket above the cylinder restraint chain.

Who orders it

Gas room operators, plant EHS managers, maintenance leads.

Rust-resistant .065 aluminum, UV-resistant print, pre-drilled in all four corners. Made in the USA. Related standards and practice to review for your site: ANSI Z535.4 CAUTION; OSHA 1910.212 machine guarding practice. A sign supports your site procedures; it does not replace training or supervision.

column3:
Frosted Valve, Cold Surface. This CAUTION Purger Expansion Valve sign from CGAP Safety reads: PURGER EXPANSION VALVE / COLD SURFACE / WEAR GLOVES. Written for cold storage warehouses, food processing plants, ice rinks and distribution centers.

Why this sign matters

Warns of a burn from a hot or very cold surface at the purger expansion valve and protects refrigeration techs, operators and visitors from minor or moderate injury.

Where to post it

Mount on the bracket at the purger expansion valve, at eye level where it is read before the task starts.

Who orders it

Refrigeration technicians and plant engineers at ammonia refrigeration facilities.

Rust-resistant .065 aluminum, UV-resistant print, pre-drilled in all four corners. Made in the USA. Related standards and practice to review for your site: ANSI Z535.4 CAUTION; site practice for hot and cold surfaces. A sign supports your site procedures; it does not replace training or supervision.
